name: Whirlpool
label: Revelation
lede: Two guys who worked at Revelation wanted a Pixies-style band with a man and a woman singing, made two records, and then lost their drummer and a guitarist to Sense Field's Warner Bros. deal.

eras.title: Jamming in a Revelation co-worker's house
eras.text: Rodney Sellars had more songs than Sense Field could use. Travis Guichard of Mean Season and Outspoken, a co-worker at Revelation, had a house to play them in. Sellars was deep into the Pixies and wanted a man and a woman on vocals.

years.h: Two Revelation employees start a band in a house
years.p: Sense Field guitarist Sellars and Guichard jam at Guichard's place twice a week. Brothers Travis Laws (bass) and Brandon Laws (drums) join, along with singer Rachel Stolte.
years.xp: Laws was one of Sellars's roommates and had played bass in [[Final Conflict|dc6848f9-0eda-4981-b5ca-f113d9658c2e]] for years, so he was, in Guichard's words, an easy fix. Sellars wanted the male/female vocal blend of the Pixies, which is how Stolte came in.

years.h: Whirlpool arrives on Revelation, 2,984 copies on black
years.p: The self-titled debut LP has a video for "Blinding Light", directed by Jim Brown. Another 305 copies of the first press are on green vinyl.

years.cap: Flyer for Farside, Mouthpiece, Whirlpool, Kill Holiday and the Suppression Swing at the Troubadour, Hollywood, December 29, 1995
years.h: One US tour, sharing bills with Deadguy and Braid
years.p: Whirlpool tour the US once, in summer 1995. Guichard says it helped to play with [[Iceburn|b3aa7443-5572-4c1f-99e5-a91e13cd3e5b]], [[Engine Kid|899baef6-af48-4caa-aff6-c1562a5dc12d]], [[Deadguy|311e7afe-e0e3-476a-a703-fcd61dc049ac]], [[Shades Apart|3f6c4af4-bb50-4672-998e-5e806b696fb3]], [[Braid|12269eae-3c21-4586-acf2-6cb03c92f4e7]] and [[Texas Is the Reason|b93c736f-a82f-4cae-9e57-a60b12d7055f]].
A CMJ Music Marathon showcase at CBGB is Whirlpool's one East Coast trip.

eras.title: The most Revelation had ever spent in a studio
eras.text: Revelation put more behind Whirlpool's second record than behind any LP before it. Then Sense Field signed to Warner Bros., and two of the band's members belonged to both.

years.h: Sense Field's drummer takes the stool
years.p: [[Scott McPherson|c857aba4-942d-448c-b172-7807647c648d]], Sellars's bandmate in Sense Field, plays drums on Liquid Glass in place of Brandon Laws.

q: We had a great relationship with Jordan Cooper and Revelation.
years.h: Liquid Glass goes to For The Record with Jim Monroe
years.p: Monroe and the band produce it, and Guichard believes it was the most Revelation ever spent on studio time for an LP. Revelation REV 52.
years.xp:
Twelve songs, including "Machine Religion", "Wasteland", "Deutchland" and one called "Cindy Crawford Pumpkin". Ed Kampworth adds keyboards on some tracks. Revelation pitched it to fans of the Pixies and X.

A second press included 110 copies on blue vinyl.

years.big: Warner signed Sense Field. Whirlpool paid for it.
years.src: No Echo: Travis Guichard · Wikipedia: Sense Field
years.h: Warner Bros. signs Sense Field, and Whirlpool stops
years.p: McPherson and Sellars can't do both bands. Guichard says Whirlpool just couldn't continue, and he was at peace with it.
years.xp: It was mutual, and nobody fell out. The members stayed friends and kept playing together off and on. Warner then left Sense Field in limbo for five years.

eras.title: Back in the garage
eras.text: Nearly twenty years on, two Whirlpool founders were under one roof again.

years.h: Guichard moves into Sellars's house, and the garage fills up
years.p: Back in the US after years in Europe, Guichard spends most of his time writing and recording in Sellars's garage. None of it has been released.
